The audit adds a rubric, meaning a set of explicit criteria: vague abstraction, unnecessary jargon, empty emphasis, repeated conclusions, padded construction, formulaic framing, stacked hedges and unclear references. An issue must have a quote and a local explanation. Zero is allowed. Duplicate or overlapping quoted spans count once; absent quotes remain available for inspection but do not enter the located count.
pair.after: The **eight habits** are vague abstraction, unnecessary jargon, empty emphasis, repeated conclusion, padded construction, formulaic framing, stacked hedges and unclear reference. The audit allows zero instances and says that a needed technical term, a justified hedge or a heading is not a fault on its own. The slop audit therefore changes two things at once: it adds the words "AI slop" and it adds the list of habits. Its effect on scores is the effect of both together.

pair.before:
A data scientist builds intuition by running experiments. You take a new tool, or one you already use, and go deep
on it: set up conditions that show where it works and where it fails, how long it takes to build, how hard it is to
get right, what it costs, and how much accuracy a given amount of effort buys. Before you train or post-train a
model, you try several candidates on your own task and keep the one that holds up.

AI coding agents make this much cheaper. You describe an experiment, an agent builds and runs it, and you read the
results and decide what to try next. Experiments that each took days by hand can now run side by side, so you can
test more hypotheses, and test each one more carefully.

This repo collects such experiments. Each notebook asks one question and answers it with measurements, failures
included.
